title: When the Archive Falls
premise: Paloma Winterbourne smuggles forbidden memories between the orbital stations and the dying colony of Meridian's Rest, whose slow abandonment has become their private archive of grief. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Paloma decodes it as an inheritance: proof that the war consuming the system was manufactured by the very institutions that now demand the colony's final evacuation. To deliver the message that could end the war — or ignite it — Paloma must choose between surrendering the archive to duty-bound authorities who will bury it, or broadcasting it illegally and losing everything they love. In the end, Paloma broadcasts from the colony itself as it goes dark, turning its last recorded breath into the message that topples the war's architects.
about_author: Beatrix Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned settlement records before turning to fiction. They write about memory, obligation, and the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Bloodstream
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs, memories hidden in neural shunts, establishes Paloma's world, their partner-in-crime Sefu, and the quiet desperation of Meridian's Rest below. Beat: competence masking dread.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. On the surface, Paloma records elder Ilsa Renn's failing memories of the colony's founding — the last fluent speaker of a dead trade-tongue. The emotional beat is tenderness tangled with guilt; Paloma profits from a death they cannot stop.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A distress signal arrives encoded in the extinct language only Ilsa still speaks. Customs flags the transmission; Paloma must decide whether to report it or decode it alone. Beat: the first crack in their careful neutrality.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The old woman translates fragments: the signal names names — architects of the war — and claims the colony itself was built to bury the evidence. Ilsa feels purpose return to her dying days. Beat: grim awakening.

chapters.title: Customs Officer Vale
chapters.summary: POV Odile Vale, customs investigator. Vale traces the illegal signal to Winterbourne and requests a warrant, but her superiors' urgency unsettles her — they want the signal destroyed, not investigated. Beat: doubt planted in the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Weight of Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Sefu urges selling the decoded message to the highest bidder; Paloma realizes Ilsa intended it for them — an inheritance, not merchandise. First flashback to Paloma's family lost in the war's opening strike. Beat: grief becomes resolve.

chapters.title: Three Buyers
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma tests the market discreetly: the Admiralty, a syndicate, and a dissident historian network all want the message — for three different wars. Every buyer is a trap. Beat: paranoia tightening.

chapters.title: Raid on the Long Gallery
chapters.summary: POV Vale. Vale raids the colony's memory-archive hall but finds it already stripped — Paloma moved everything. She discovers evidence her own agency helped erase the colony's records years ago. Beat: antagonist's loyalty fractures.

chapters.title: Sefu's Price
chapters.summary: POV Sefu. Cornered by the syndicate, Sefu betrays the archive's location to save his brother held hostage — then immediately regrets it and sends Paloma a coded warning. Beat: love against survival, betrayal with a conscience.

chapters.title: Running the Dark Lane
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A desperate flight through unpatrolled space with the full archive aboard, pursued by both Admiralty and syndicate ships. Paloma realizes the message can't be delivered — it must be broadcast. Beat: plan crystallizes under fire.

chapters.title: Vale Defects
chapters.summary: POV Vale. Confronting her director, Vale learns the war's origin was sanctioned at the highest level. She burns her career, steals the decryption key fragment, and goes looking for Winterbourne. Beat: duty inverted into justice.

chapters.title: Two Smugglers, One Truth
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma and Vale meet in a derelict station, adversaries forced into alliance. Mutual contempt curdles into wary respect — and something warmer neither will name. Beat: the love thread ignites.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Last Recording
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Dying, Ilsa records the complete translation and a personal testament for whoever hears it. Her chapter is quiet, elegiac — the colony's whole history distilled into one voice. Beat: the heart of the book.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Collects
chapters.summary: POV Sefu. The syndicate takes Sefu's brother anyway and comes for Paloma. Sefu chooses redemption, feeding the syndicate false coordinates at lethal cost to himself. Beat: sacrifice as atonement.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Meridian's Gate
chapters.summary: POV Vale. The Admiralty blockades the colony, officially an 'evacuation,' actually a containment. Vale's stolen key gets them through, but she is now a traitor with a price on her head. Beat: no way back.

chapters.title: What the Archive Holds
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Inside the colony's deep vault, Paloma finds the physical proof beneath the memories: the war was commissioned to seize the colony's rare-element fields. The message isn't just testimony — it's a detonator. Beat: revelation.

chapters.title: Evacuation Order
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The government orders Meridian's Rest emptied in forty-eight hours; holdouts refuse to leave their dead. Paloma must convince the colonists that staying to broadcast is worth dying for — or choose for them. Beat: impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Night Before the End
chapters.summary: POV Paloma and Vale, alternating. A stolen night among the last colonists: songs in the dead tongue, confessions, Vale and Paloma finally admitting what they are to each other. Beat: love fully claimed on the eve of ruin.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. As the fleet moves in, Paloma transmits the archive on every open channel — Ilsa's voice, the proof, the names. Stations go silent, then erupt. The war's architecture cracks in public view. Beat: climax, truth as weapon.

chapters.title: The Fleet Turns
chapters.summary: POV Vale. Mutiny spreads through the blockade; crews refuse the bombardment order. Vale stands on the colony's roof as the guns power down, arrested but victorious. Beat: justice outside the law, won.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Tribunals begin; the architects fall. Paloma, hollowed by Ilsa's death and Sefu's sacrifice, wanders the silent colony and finds peace in the emptiness — the archive did what archives do: it outlived them. Beat: grief transmuted.

chapters.title: When the Archive Falls
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Months later, Paloma and Vale reopen Meridian's Rest as a free archive where anyone's memory may be stored and heard. Paloma adds their own recording beside Ilsa's. Final beat: inheritance fulfilled — love outlasting duty.
